Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, released by Anthropic on 9 November 2026, are supported, with fast mode and prices. A fast-mode request no longer pauses subscription accounts, and the Usage page keeps past days and months after retention deletes their records.

## Changes

- **Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2.**
  - `claude-fable-5-2` is in the Claude model list. Mythos 5.2 (`claude-mythos-5-2`) is for organizations Anthropic has verified, so it shows only on accounts whose model list includes it.
  - Fast mode (`speed: "fast"`) is sent for both models, where Anthropic offers it at twice the standard price. Before, Fusebox removed it as unsupported. Subscriptions follow `claude-subscription-fast-mode`, below.
  - A translated request that forces a tool goes to these models with `tool_choice: auto`, since they refuse a forced choice. The parallel-call limit stays.
  - Prices: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, $0.20 cache reads, $10 five-minute and $16 one-hour cache writes, and double for fast mode (catalogue t3-2026-11-09.1, rate card 2026-11-09.1).
    - LiteLLM doesn't list these models yet, so the estimate uses Anthropic's published rates and says so (`published_provider_rate_fallback`).
    - Requests stored without a price are priced at the first start.
  - Fable 5.2's thinking only works in the account that produced it. A conversation that moves to another account continues without its earlier reasoning.
  - Fusebox passes tool definitions through unchanged. A client that sends the old `computer_20251124` tool, or an advisor other than Fable or Mythos 5.2, gets Anthropic's 400 from these models.
  - [docs/model-support-2026-11-09.md](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/blob/v0.15.0/docs/model-support-2026-11-09.md) has the details.
- **Fast mode on subscriptions.** A subscription bills fast mode to usage credits only. Without credits, Anthropic refuses it with a 429 that Fusebox took for a spent account: each account it tried had Opus paused until the next usage check, and the error named a month-long wait.
  - Signed-in Claude accounts now get fast requests at standard speed unless `claude-subscription-fast-mode` is on (off by default; a switch under Connections). Models without fast mode get standard speed on every account. The `fast-mode` beta flag stays, as on Claude Code's own standard-speed retries.
  - The request details list the change under "Dropped".
  - A 429 whose reset is the monthly billing boundary no longer sets a cooldown that long, and any reset Fusebox reads from those headers is capped at a week.
  - Claude 429s, and errors on fast requests, log a "Claude refusal" line. It has the rate-limit headers, the error type and known phrases, never the message.
- **Usage kept as totals.** Retention used to delete the 15-minute rollups along with each request's record, so past days and months disappeared from the Usage page.
  - Retention now keeps those records' totals: calls, cost, every token category, and the partial and unpriced counts with their reasons, by provider, model, account, client, source and Claude Code entrypoint. Every past day and month reads the same after its records are gone, in every time zone and with every filter.
  - Traffic like production's keeps about 0.2 MB of totals a day, where its records take about 34 MB.
  - `usage.totals-retention-days` bounds the totals; 0, the default, keeps them.
  - Nothing is counted twice. That includes a proxy call and its imported copy that fall on either side of the cutoff.
  - The Usage page has a 12-month preset, a Day / Month switch on the chart (months by default past three), custom dates back 10 years, and a note on days kept as totals.
  - Status measures the totals apart from the records and estimates where the database size levels off. Changing `warn-database-mb` no longer asks for a restart.

## Upgrading

- **Database.** The usage database stays on schema 5.
  - The first start adds six empty tables: `usage_history`, `_entrypoints`, `_facets`, `_dims`, `_matches` and `_responses`. It adds no triggers.
  - v0.14.0 ignores those tables. But if v0.14.0 runs a purge after you go back, it deletes records without keeping their totals, which leaves a gap on the Usage page.
- **New settings:** `claude-subscription-fast-mode` (off by default) and `usage.totals-retention-days` (0 keeps totals for good). v0.14.0 ignores both.
- **Fast mode on subscriptions.** A client that relied on fast mode through a subscription with usage credits needs `claude-subscription-fast-mode: true`.
- **API changes:**
  - Request `control_downgrades` can hold `speed_fast_subscription` and `speed_fast_unsupported_model`.
  - The usage dashboard reports `summarized_before_ms`.
  - `POST /api/usage/retention` also removes kept totals before its date.
- **Pricing.** Catalogues t3-2026-11-09.1 and 2026-11-09.1 only add the Fable and Mythos 5.2 rows; no other price changes.

## Known issue

- **SQLite advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0459 ([#60](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/issues/60)).** The bundled SQLite is still 3.50.2. Before 3.54.0, SQLite can return stale memory when it opens a database together with a crafted `-wal` file of a different page size. Fusebox opens only its own usage database, so this matters only where someone less trusted can write files next to it. The fix (rusqlite 0.41, SQLite 3.54.1) made usage inserts about four times slower in testing, so it waits for a later release.

Validation: 1,004 Rust tests (12 ignored), 183 dashboard tests and 46 Python tests passed, and CI passed on Linux, macOS and Windows. The dependency audit fails only on the advisory above. Production has run the fast-mode and usage-totals changes since 8 November 2026. Fable 5.2 support isn't in production yet.

[Full comparison with v0.14.0](https://github.com/DigitalPals/Fusebox/compare/v0.14.0...v0.15.0).
